name: Georgia
summary: A large red cross of St George on white, with a smaller red bolnur-katskhuri cross in each quarter. Based on medieval Georgian banners, it was the flag of Mikheil Saakashvili's United National Movement and was adopted after the Rose Revolution of 2003.
origin: A white banner with a red cross is associated with the medieval Kingdom of Georgia; a flag with a large cross and four smaller crosses appears in a 14th-century map by the Genoese cartographer Pietro Vesconte, labelled at Tbilisi.

The Georgian Democratic Republic (1918–1921) and independent Georgia from 1990 used a dark red flag with black and white stripes in the canton. The five-cross flag was revived by nationalists in the 1990s, used in the Rose Revolution of November 2003, and adopted by Parliament on 14 January 2004.

colors.name: Red

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Commonly read as innocence, purity and wisdom.

symbols.name: Cross of St George
symbols.description: A large red cross across the whole flag.
symbols.meaning: St George, Georgia's patron saint, and Christianity.

symbols.name: Four bolnur-katskhuri crosses
symbols.description: Smaller red crosses with flared ends in each quarter.
symbols.meaning: Christian symbolism; commonly said to represent the Five Wounds or Jesus and the four Evangelists.

history.label: Democratic Republic of Georgia
history.note: Dark red with black and white canton stripes.

facts: The flag of the Kingdom of Jerusalem used the same five-cross layout in gold on white.
The Five Cross Flag was the party flag of the United National Movement before becoming the national flag.
clues: A large red cross on white with four smaller red crosses in the quarters.
Adopted after a revolution named after a flower in 2003.
A version is shown on a 14th-century map at the city of Tbilisi.
Its large cross is that of the nation's patron saint.
